notes.name: case_narrative
notes.text: A 30-year-old, gravida-six, para-five, with a history of gestational hyper-tension, reported to the emergency room at 36 weeks gestation with com- plaints of abdominal cramping and light vaginal bleeding during the past 12 hours. At time of first assessment, foetal heart tones were detected. The uterus was tense, irritable, and tender. The mother was hypotensive with tachycardia. A presumptive diagnosis of abruptio placenta was made, and an emergency caesarean section was performed under general anaesthesia. The baby was stillborn. The mother continued to bleed from her uterus and phlebotomy sites and went into profound shock secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation. Despite administration of blood and clot- ting factors, intravascular pressure could not be maintained, and the mother died on the operating table. Maternal autopsy confirmed the clinical diagnosis.
